<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 6 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Covariant Derivative</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">6.3</span> Parallel Transport and Autoparallels</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Let <span class="math inline">\(\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathcal{M}\)</span> be a smooth curve, with velocity <span class="math inline">\(v_\gamma : \lambda \mapsto v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\)</span>. Since the direction of <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> is a single tangent vector, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{v_{\gamma(\lambda)}} \mathcal{Y}\)</span> is defined for every <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span>. The quantities one wants to differentiate along <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span>, however, starting with <span class="math inline">\(v_\gamma\)</span> itself, are not vector fields on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, but <strong>vector fields along</strong> <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span>, i.e. maps  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathcal{X}_\gamma : \mathbb{R} &amp;\longrightarrow T\mathcal{M} \\
            \lambda                         &amp;\longmapsto \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda) \in T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M},
        \end{align*}</span>  whose component functions <span class="math inline">\(x^i_\gamma(\lambda) \coloneqq (dx^i)_{\gamma(\lambda)}\big( \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda) \big)\)</span> are smooth (for those <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\gamma(\lambda) \in \mathcal{U}\)</span>). Examples are the velocity <span class="math inline">\(v_\gamma\)</span>, with component functions <span class="math inline">\(\dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)\)</span>, and the restriction <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y} \circ \gamma\)</span> of a vector field <span class="math inline">\(\left. \mathcal{Y} \right|_\mathcal{U} = \tilde{x}^j \, \partial x_j\)</span>, with component functions <span class="math inline">\(\tilde{x}^j \circ \gamma\)</span>. The converse fails: if <span class="math inline">\(\gamma(\lambda_1) = \gamma(\lambda_2)\)</span> but <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda_1) \neq \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda_2)\)</span>, as for the velocity of a figure-eight curve at its crossing point, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma\)</span> is not the restriction of any vector field on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> cannot be applied to it directly.</p></li>
<li><p>There exists a unique operator <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{v_\gamma}\)</span>, the <strong>covariant derivative along</strong> <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span>, mapping smooth vector fields along <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> to smooth vector fields along <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span>, such that, for all <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma, \mathcal{Y}_\gamma\)</span> along <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\)</span> and smooth <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\)</span>:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em><span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}\)</span>-linearity:</em> <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{v_\gamma} (\mathcal{X}_\gamma + \alpha \, \mathcal{Y}_\gamma) = \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma + \alpha \, \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{Y}_\gamma\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Leibniz rule:</em>  <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{v_\gamma} (\textrm{\runic ᚱ} \, \mathcal{X}_\gamma) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}' \, \mathcal{X}_\gamma + \textrm{\runic ᚱ} \, \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Compatibility with <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>:</em> if <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = \mathcal{Y} \circ \gamma\)</span>, then <span class="math inline">\(\big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \nabla_{v_{\gamma(\lambda)}} \mathcal{Y}\)</span>.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>In a chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\)</span> it reads  <span class="math display">\begin{equation*}
            \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \Big( \frac{d x^k_\gamma}{d\lambda}(\lambda)
            + \left(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\right)^k_{ji}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, x^j_\gamma(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \Big)
            (\partial x_k)_{\gamma(\lambda)}.
            \tag{$\ast\ast$}
        \end{equation*}</span>  <em>Proof.</em> As for <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma\)</span> at <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span> only depends on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma\)</span> near <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span>, so it suffices to work on an interval of parameters along which <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> stays in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>. <em>Uniqueness:</em> there, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = x^j_\gamma \, (\partial x_j \circ \gamma)\)</span>, so properties 1 and 2, then 3, and finally property 4 of <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> force  <span class="math display">\[
            \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda)
            = \frac{d x^j_\gamma}{d\lambda}(\lambda) \, (\partial x_j)_{\gamma(\lambda)}
            + x^j_\gamma(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \nabla_{(\partial x_i)_{\gamma(\lambda)}} \partial x_j,
        \]</span>  which is <span class="math inline">\((\ast\ast)\)</span>. <em>Existence:</em> define <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{v_\gamma}\)</span> chart by chart through <span class="math inline">\((\ast\ast)\)</span>. Properties 1 and 2 are immediate. For property 3, the expansion of <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\mathcal{X}_p} \mathcal{Y}\)</span> derived above, at <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_p = v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\)</span>, coincides with <span class="math inline">\((\ast\ast)\)</span> for <span class="math inline">\(x^j_\gamma = \tilde{x}^j \circ \gamma\)</span>, since <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma(\lambda)}(\tilde{x}^k) = (\tilde{x}^k \circ \gamma)'(\lambda)\)</span>. On chart overlaps, both chart expressions satisfy properties 1–3, so by uniqueness they coincide. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p></li>
<li><p>We define, for all <span class="math inline">\(\lambda \in \mathbb{R}\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\[
            \begin{array}{c|c}
                \begin{array}{c}
                    \text{A vector field } \mathcal{X}_\gamma \text{ along } \gamma \text{ is}\\
                    \text{\textbf{parallelly transported} along } \gamma \text{ if}
                \end{array}
                &amp;
                \begin{array}{c}
                    \text{A smooth curve } \gamma \text{ is}\\
                    \text{\textbf{autoparallelly transported} if}
                \end{array} \\[8pt]
                \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma = 0.
                &amp;
                \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma = 0.
                \\[12pt] \hline \\[-6pt]
                \begin{array}{c}
                    \text{A vector field } \mathcal{X}_\gamma \text{ along } \gamma \text{ is}\\
                    \text{\textbf{parallel} along } \gamma \text{ if}
                \end{array}
                &amp;
                \begin{array}{c}
                    \text{A smooth curve } \gamma \text{ is}\\
                    \text{\textbf{autoparallel} if}
                \end{array} \\[8pt]
                \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, \mathcal{X}_\gamma(\lambda).
                &amp;
                \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, v_{\gamma(\lambda)}.
            \end{array}
        \]</span>  where <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\)</span> is a smooth function. We define the <strong>acceleration</strong> of the curve <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> as <span class="math inline">\(a_\gamma(\lambda) \coloneqq \big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma \big)(\lambda) \in T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M}\)</span>. Parallel transport cannot, in general, be phrased in terms of vector fields on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>: transporting a vector around a closed curve typically returns a different vector, so the transported vectors are not the values of any single vector field on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>. This failure to return, the <strong>holonomy</strong> of <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>, is closely related to the curvature introduced below.</p></li>
<li><p>Applying <span class="math inline">\((\ast\ast)\)</span> to <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = v_\gamma\)</span>, whose component functions are <span class="math inline">\(x^k_\gamma = \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(\frac{d}{d\lambda} \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) = \big( \mathscr{X}^k \circ \gamma \big)''(\lambda) \eqqcolon \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)\)</span>, and using that the <span class="math inline">\((\partial x_k)_{\gamma(\lambda)}\)</span> form a basis of <span class="math inline">\(T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M}\)</span>, the autoparallel condition <span class="math inline">\(\big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma \big)(\lambda) = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\)</span> becomes the <strong>autoparallel equation</strong>  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \left(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\right)^k_{ji}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
        \end{align*}</span>  which, for autoparallelly transported curves (<span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚱ} \equiv 0\)</span>), reads  <span class="math display" id="eq_autoparallel">\begin{equation}
            \boxed{
                \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \left(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\right)^k_{ji}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) = 0,
            } \tag{6.1}
        \end{equation}</span>  a system of <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span> second-order ordinary differential equations for the chart representative <span class="math inline">\((\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma)(\lambda)\)</span>. When all the <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma_\mathscr{X}\)</span>’s vanish, as for the Euclidean plane in the cartesian chart with its standard connection, its solutions are straight lines.</p></li>
</ul>
